# Ollama `:cloud` Anthropic-compat: Kimi K2.5 native tokens leak, nested objects stringified on Qwen/GLM

## Summary

Using Ollama 0.20.7 as an Anthropic Messages API shim (`/v1/messages` endpoint) with `:cloud` models, two related bugs break multi-agent tool-calling workflows (Claude Code agent teams):

1. **Kimi K2.5 native tool-call tokens pass through as plain text.** The model emits `<|tool_call_begin|>functions.X:0<|tool_call_argument_begin|>{…}<|tool_call_end|><|tool_calls_section_end|>` in what becomes an assistant `text` block instead of a properly-formed `tool_use` block. Subsequent requests replay the transcript and the Anthropic validator rejects with `"tool_use block missing required 'name' field"`.

2. **Nested JSON objects in tool-call parameters get serialized as strings on Qwen3.x, GLM-5/5.1 (and others).** The model emits `{"message": {"type": "shutdown_response", …}}` but the response arrives with `"message": "{\"type\":\"shutdown_response\",…}"` (a JSON string). Anthropic's validator then requires `summary` because `typeof message === 'string'`, and any downstream dispatch keyed on `message.type` (structured protocol messages) never fires.

Both failure modes break Claude Code's `SendMessage` tool and the `shutdown_request` / `shutdown_response` lifecycle for in-process teammates.

## Environment

- Ollama: `0.20.7`
- Backend: Ollama Cloud (`:cloud` model variants — `remote_host: https://ollama.com:443`)
- Client: Claude Code `2.1.110` with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434` and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=ollama`
- Platform: WSL2 (Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2)

| Model | Plain-text `SendMessage` | Structured shutdown_response | Failure mode |
|---|---|---|---|

The Qwen3.6 [chat template](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B/blob/main/chat_template.jinja) supports a `preserve_thinking` flag that preserves reasoning across all turns:

{%- endif %}

items.title: Tool-parameter JSON-Schema constraints (minimum/maximum/default/…) silently dropped at parse time
items.body:
### What is happening

JSON-Schema validation keywords on tool parameters are silently discarded when a `/api/chat` request is parsed, so they never reach the model. `type`, `description`, `enum`, `anyOf`, `items`, `properties`, and `required` survive; everything else — `minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum`, `multipleOf`, `default`, `format`, `pattern`, `minLength`/`maxLength`, `minItems`/`maxItems`, `const` — is dropped.

### Root cause

The drop is at unmarshal time, before any chat template runs. `api.ToolProperty` (`api/types.go`) has fields only for `AnyOf`, `Type`, `Items`, `Description`, `Enum`, `Properties`, `Required`:

```go
type ToolProperty struct {
	AnyOf       []ToolProperty     `json:"anyOf,omitempty"`
	Type        PropertyType       `json:"type,omitempty"`
	Items       any                `json:"items,omitempty"`
	Description string             `json:"description,omitempty"`
	Enum        []any              `json:"enum,omitempty"`
	Properties  *ToolPropertiesMap `json:"properties,omitempty"`
	Required    []string           `json:"required,omitempty"`
}
```

`json.Unmarshal` drops any key without a matching struct field, so a keyword like `minimum` on an incoming tool param is gone before the model template is ever invoked. This is template-independent — it affects every model. `ToolFunctionParameters` similarly has no place for these keywords.

## What happens

gemma4 (tested: `gemma4:26b-a4b-it-q4_K_M`) sometimes emits tool-call arguments as
`save_as='report.docx'` or `save_as="report.docx"` instead of the canonical
`save_as:<|"|>report.docx<|"|>`. When it does, parsing fails and the API returns
**`tool_calls: []` with empty `content`** — the generated arguments survive only in the
server's warning log, so the client cannot recover or retry intelligently.

Server log:

```
gemma4 tool call parsing failed: invalid character 's' looking for beginning of object key string
repair failed to produce valid JSON arguments
```

`quoteGemma4BareKeys` (model/parsers/gemma4.go) only recognises a bare key when it is
followed by `:`; there is no handling of `=` anywhere in the parser, so the key is left
unquoted and `json.Unmarshal` fails. `repairGemma4SingleQuotedValues` is also anchored on
`:`, so both recovery paths miss the same case. The renderer emits `:` canonically, but
the model drifts to `=` — in our runs, most often when the *user prompt* itself contains
quoted `key='value'` assignments (68% parse success vs ~95% with a plain prompt, n=22/20).

## Summary

When a tool has a parameter whose JSON schema is `array<object>` (e.g. `[{"type":"web"}]`) and the model (Qwen3 family using the `TAG_WITH_TAGGED` / `<tool_call><function=...><parameter=...>` format) emits it as the inner value of a `<parameter>` tag, the autoparser's PEG `p.json()` fails mid-stream. Two cascading problems follow:

1. **Root parse failure.** `build_tool_parser_tag_tagged` uses `p.json()` for any parameter that doesn't resolve to a string schema. On array-of-object values the PEG parser aborts, the request ends in a 500 with `Failed to parse input at pos N: <tool_call>...`.
2. **Partial state leaked to the client.** Before the failure, the partial-parse fallback at `common/chat.cpp:2158` returns whatever AST was built so far. For streaming (`is_partial=true`) this surfaces to the client as an SSE delta containing `tool_calls[0].function.arguments = "{"` (one character). The client, acting correctly per the OpenAI spec, appends this tool_call to conversation history.
3. **History poisoning.** Every subsequent request replays that history. `func_args_not_string` at `common/chat.cpp:1842-1860` eagerly parses `tool_calls[].function.arguments` as JSON and throws a 500 on the bare `{`, so the conversation is now stuck: every follow-up crashes with `Failed to parse tool call arguments as JSON: ... unexpected end of input`, even though the client did nothing wrong.

Net effect: a single tool-call attempt with a complex parameter permanently wedges the conversation until the client manually strips the assistant message from history.

Duplicate rule definitions in generated GBNF grammar with large `tools` list (harmony/gpt-oss) → "failed to parse grammar"

## Description

When sending a chat completion request with a large `tools` array (17 function definitions, none using `$ref`/`$defs`) to `llama-server` running `gpt-oss-120b` (harmony chat format, started with `--jinja`), the JSON-schema-to-grammar converter emits **the same GBNF rule name with an identical body twice**, and the server then fails with:

```
failed to parse grammar
Failed to initialize samplers: failed to parse grammar
```
returned as HTTP 400 to the client.

This is *not* the same as #21228 (MAX_REPETITION_THRESHOLD / `$ref` expansion) — there is no `$ref` or `$defs` anywhere in the schema, and the failure is a hard 400, not a silent fallback to unconstrained generation.

## Environment

- llama.cpp build: `b10069-178a6c449` (from `system_fingerprint` in a successful response on the same server)
- Model: `ggml-org/gpt-oss-120b-GGUF` (MXFP4 quant), harmony chat template
- Server started with `--jinja -ngl 999`
- Client: OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`, `tools` array with 17 function definitions (a coding-agent tool list — file read/write/edit/grep/glob/bash/etc.)

## What I observed

Across repeated requests with the full 17-tool list, the generated grammar (visible via server stdout/stderr) contains duplicate `::=` definitions for the same rule name. The specific rule that duplicates **varies between requests** — observed twice, in two different tools:

Run 1 (duplicate in the `todowrite` tool's array-of-objects property):

## Summary

The Qwen3-Coder chat parser (`common_chat_params_init_qwen3_coder`, added in #26252) has a documented workaround for models that omit the opening `<tool_call>` wrapper while still emitting `<function=name>`. In practice the model can deviate further than that, abandoning the structured format entirely, and the lazy grammar trigger never fires, so the response falls through as plain content instead of `tool_calls`.

## Root cause

The trigger that switches into constrained decoding only watches for a literal `<tool_call>` or `<function=` substring in the raw output stream:

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/f5919bf458ef190468b5c329bb293f8a54a1e69c/common/chat.cpp#L1241

```cpp
(reasoning << p.content(p.until_one_of({ "<tool_call>", "<function=" })) << tool_calls);
```

The existing workaround, one line above, acknowledges partial omission:

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/f5919bf458ef190468b5c329bb293f8a54a1e69c/common/chat.cpp#L1232

```cpp
// Qwen3-Coder models may occasionally omit the <tool_call> token.
```

...and makes the *first* call's `<tool_call>\n` wrapper optional in the grammar. That only helps if the model still emits `<function=`. When it emits neither trigger string at all, `p.content()` consumes the whole response as free text and the tool-call branch is never entered.

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/f5919bf458ef190468b5c329bb293f8a54a1e69c/common/chat.cpp#L3182-L3186

This proposal outlines a unified approach to tool calling in vLLM that improves robustness, reduces parser complexity, and preserves model-native behavior. It achieves this through region-scoped guided decoding with tool-aware grammars and explicit boundary tracking during generation.

Tool calling in vLLM is currently implemented via two structurally different mechanisms that lead to inconsistent behavior, reduced robustness, and increasing parser complexity.

* malformed or partially emitted tool arguments
* hallucinated tool names or incorrect tool selection
* difficulty handling streaming or partial outputs
* divergence across model-specific parsing implementations

### Summary

While comparing the Rust frontend tool-call parsers against the independent Python parsers they reimplement, I found several cases where the two produce **different tool-call arguments for identical model output**. Some of these may be intentional improvements in the Rust implementation; others look like unintended behavior changes. Filing to get maintainer guidance on which are intended before proposing fixes.

This only concerns parsers where an independent pure-Python implementation still exists. Parsers that are thin adapters over the Rust engine (kimi_k2, minimax, glm47, qwen3_engine) cannot diverge and are out of scope.

### Divergences

#### 1. Qwen3-Coder — argument type coercion (Rust coerces, Python does not)

`vllm/parser/qwen3.py:57-76` (`_qwen3_arg_converter`) emits every parameter value as a `.strip()`'d string via `json.dumps`; it has no access to the tool schema. The Rust parser (`rust/src/parser/src/tool/qwen_coder.rs` → `parameters.rs`) routes each value through schema-aware coercion.

Input (with `days: {type: integer}` in the tool schema):
```
<function=get_weather>
<parameter=days>3</parameter>
</function>
```

Arguably the Rust behavior is *more* correct (it honors the declared schema type), but it is a behavior change between the two frontends. Which is intended?

Python uses `value.strip()` (qwen3.py:65). Rust trims only a single leading/trailing newline (`trim_one_wrapping_newline`, qwen_coder.rs).

- Python → `{"location": "Dallas"}`

items.body:
# [Bug] MiniMax-M3 tool-call parser buffers arguments — no incremental streaming

## Summary
The `minimax_m3` Rust tool-call parser (`rust/src/parser/src/tool/minimax_m3.rs`) emits tool-call **arguments only after the full `<invoke>` block is parsed** — a single `ToolCallDelta` with the complete JSON. During streaming (`stream=true`), clients therefore receive **no incremental argument deltas**: the whole `function.arguments` blob arrives in one SSE chunk at the end, breaking progressive UIs (e.g. rendering a chart/slide as arguments stream).

Comparable parsers that stream fine: `kimi_k2` streams because the model emits arguments as raw JSON and the parser passes bytes through (`take_json_object`). M3 buffers because its XML `<parameter>` tags are converted to JSON schema-aware, and the current parser waits for the whole `<invoke>` to do that conversion.

## Where
`rust/src/parser/src/tool/minimax_m3.rs`:
- `MinimaxM3Event::Invoke { name, params }` — a single atomic event.
- `invoke_event()` does `take_until(0.., INVOKE_END)` to grab the entire body, then `parse_invoke_params()` over the whole body; `apply_event()` converts all params and pushes **one** `ToolCallDelta`.
- Doc comment states it: *"Arguments are emitted only after a full `<invoke>` block is parsed."*

## Reproduce
Stream a tool call and observe `choices[].delta.tool_calls[].function.arguments`:
- **M3**: 1 argument-bearing chunk (whole JSON, ~900 B, at the end).
- **Kimi K2**: many small argument fragments over time.
(Anthropic `/v1/messages` shows the same: one `input_json_delta` for M3 vs many for Kimi.)

## Proposed fix (implemented + verified on the pre-refactor `m3_release` version)
Per-parameter incremental emission, mirroring Kimi's proven name-first pattern:
1. Add `MinimaxM3Mode::InsideInvoke`; parser fields `current_tool_name: Option<String>` + `param_emitted: bool`.
2. Replace atomic `Invoke` with `InvokeStart{name}` → `Param{name, value}` (one per top-level `<parameter>`) → `InvokeEnd`.

vLLM nightly (image `vllm/vllm-openai:cu129-nightly-c71a583aa9`, also reproduced on current `main` code path), GLM-5.2 (NVFP4) on 4×GPU TP4, `--tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Under concurrent load, GLM-4.7-family models sporadically emit a tool call with the opening `<arg_value>` tag missing, while the argument value and the closing tag are fully intact:

```
<tool_call>search<arg_key>query</arg_key>how many vacation days left</arg_value></tool_call>
```

The glm47 parser matches arguments with

```python
_ARG_RE = re.compile(
    r"<arg_key>(?P<key>.*?)</arg_key>\s*"
    r"<arg_value>(?P<value>.*?)</arg_value>",
    re.DOTALL,
)
```

(`vllm/parser/glm47_moe.py`), so the malformed-but-recoverable call silently parses to `arguments: "{}"`. The client then fails schema validation for the tool (e.g. `Invalid input: expected string, received undefined`), retries typically fail the same way (the broken `{}` call gets rendered back into the chat history), and the agent degrades.

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

GLM-4.x consistently enters a seemingly-infinite generation (and consistently has EAGLE multi-token prediction failure, i.e. `accept len: 1.0`) when `tool_choice` is set to `"required"`.

I believe this is because SGLang automatically enforces using the `JsonArrayParser` when `tool_choice` is set to `"required"`:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/f6cfe9f1972d351400f0e56acc55d0af4ef3bc10/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py#L1050-L1054

Unfortunately, this is incorrect behavior, at least as far as GLM is concerned. GLM *does not use JSON* for tool calls: instead, it uses its own XML-based format, as documented here:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/f6cfe9f1972d351400f0e56acc55d0af4ef3bc10/python/sglang/srt/function_call/glm4_moe_detector.py#L46-L50

So attempting to enforce JSON output for tool calls puts the model out of distribution, and also causes the speculator to fail, since it wasn't trained on JSON tool calls (since GLM-4-MoE doesn't use them).

I suspect this is also broken for named function calling (aka, `ToolChoice` — where the caller is forcing a specific function to be called) since it's still trying to force an XML-based tool calling model into responding with JSON; and it's probably also broken for MiniMax M2, which also uses XML rather than JSON. In general it seems unsafe to assume that function/tool calls will be JSON-based for all models: `JsonArrayParser` should probably only be used for `response_format: "json_object"`.

cc @CatherineSu

## Motivation

Tool call tests today only cover a small model (Llama-3.2-1B in `test/registered/openai_server/function_call/test_openai_function_calling.py`). Large models like DeepSeek V3.2 have no tool call coverage in CI, so bugs like #17593 and #17551 only get caught when users hit them. This issue tracks adding tool call tests to the nightly 8-GPU suite.

## Scenarios

These should be common across all models that support tool calling:

**Basic**
1. Format check — `tool_calls` is a non-empty list, `function.name` / `function.arguments` present, arguments is valid JSON, `finish_reason` is `"tool_calls"`
2. Field placement — tool call goes in `tool_calls`, not `content` (#17593)
3. Streaming — chunks concatenate to valid JSON, `finish_reason` correct

**tool_choice**

4. `"required"` — always returns tool call
5. `"none"` — never returns tool call
6. Specific function — returns the specified one

**Multi-turn**

7. Tool result follow-up — pass tool result back, model replies based on it
8. Thinking + tool call — after tool result, output in `content` not `reasoning_content` (#17551, DeepSeek specific for now — might be model-internal, will write the test first and see)

**Other**

9. Parallel tool calls — multiple tool calls in one request
10. Strict mode — `strict: true` enforces schema

### Describe the bug

When using `--tool-call-parser kimi_k2` with `stream: true`, the SSE `tool_calls[].function.arguments` chunks produce concatenated JSON that contains invalid escape sequences (e.g. `\(`, `\|`, `\'`). The same request with `stream: false` returns valid JSON.

This is a **streaming-only** bug — the chunking path in the parser corrupts backslash escape sequences, likely by splitting `\\` pairs across chunk boundaries so that one `\` ends up at the end of one chunk and the character after it (e.g. `(`, `|`, `'`) starts the next, producing an invalid JSON escape in the concatenated result.

### Observed behavior

Concatenating the streamed `tool_calls[].function.arguments` fragments produces a string that fails `json.loads()` with errors like:

The critical run that isolates the parser bug:

```

  B (non-stream + tools): PASS    ← model JSON is valid
  C (stream, no tools)  : PASS

  -> STREAMING PARSER BUG: model produced valid JSON (B=PASS)

### Describe the bug

The Qwen3 Coder tool-call parser currently buffers string parameter values until it sees `</parameter>` or another terminating tag.

## Describe the bug

When a tool's `parameters` uses a top-level `oneOf` (a common JSON-Schema composition), SGLang's
MiniMax-M3 tool-call parser fails to resolve the per-branch property schemas. As a result the emitted
`tool_calls[].function.arguments` have the wrong types:

- a `number` argument is returned as a **string** (`{"number": "42"}` instead of `{"number": 42}`)
- an `array` argument **leaks the model's raw internal parser tags** as a plain string
  (`{"stringList": "]<]minimax[>[<item>12]<]minimax[>[</item>..."}` instead of `{"stringList": ["12","34"]}`)

This is caught by MiniMax's official verifier test
`m3_format_check/m3_text_tests.py::TestToolCallSchema::test_14_07_oneof_toplevel_schema_stream`.

Serve MiniMax-M3 with tool-call parsing enabled:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser auto \
  --tool-call-parser auto \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --port 8043
